title: The affine-line localization triangle in projective coordinates
statement: Let A be a finite commutative ring, N a positive integer annihilating A, S a Noetherian scheme on which N is invertible, t an ordinary finite Tate transport, and D a normalized projective-line adjunction datum [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction]. In the ordinary derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], use the functors and adjunctions of [def-amb-affine-trace-construction]. For every complex K on S, put F=Rq_* for the projective-line projection q, J the standard affine-chart adjunction, and M the projective right functor applied to K. There exist a complex B on S, maps r:F(M) to B and w:B to (F J_! J^* M)[1], and an isomorphism b:B direct-sum K to F(M), such that (F of the open counit, r, w) is a distinguished triangle, the first injection followed by b and r is the identity of B, and b followed by the normalized projective counit is second projection. The Lean attachment specifies all maps and compositions, with no boundedness hypothesis on K.

proof.text: Let q be the projective projection, j its standard affine chart and i the infinity section. Tensor the given normalized projective-line decomposition with K. The additive tensor functor preserves biproducts. Combine its inverse biproduct comparison, tensoring the decomposition, the tensor-unit comparison and the proper projection isomorphism to obtain b₀:B₀⊕K≅Rq_*M with B₀=K tensor A_S(1)[2]. The datum counit normalization, functoriality, and biproduct identities give b₀ followed by the actual projective counit equal to second projection.

The proved tensorProjectionAdjunct calculation identifies the first injection followed by b₀ with the adjoint of the canonical pullback/tensor/shifted-line isomorphism q*B₀≅M. This uses the defining first component of the decomposition and the inverse-image adjunction identity.

Keep the closed vertex B=Rq_*Ri_*i*M and let r=Rq_* of the closed adjunction unit at M. The source-library leftDerivedUpperStarCompSectionIso and exact/derived inverse-image comparison identify q* then i* with identity, since i≫q=id. The composite adjunction therefore has invertible unit. Naturality of the closed unit rewrites the first injection followed by b₀ and r as this composite unit followed by direct image of i* of the isomorphism q*B₀≅M. Thus this first-coordinate map B₀→B is invertible. Precompose b₀ by the biproduct of its inverse with identity on K. This gives b:B⊕K≅Rq_*M and both required coordinate equations; it needs no explicit finite-direct-image composition comparison.

Apply exists_distTriang_openClosed to j and i, complementary by ProjectiveLine.range_infinity. The infinity section is a closed immersion because its composite with the separated projection is identity. Apply the triangulated direct image Rq_* to the distinguished triangle. Transport the first vertex through the exact/derived open inverse-image comparison and the shift of its inverse at the connecting morphism. The ofNatIsoRight counit formula identifies the transported first arrow with Rq_* of the specified affineTraceOpenAdjunction counit. Return this triangle and the normalized b from the preceding steps.

lean.statement:
theorem affineTraceLine_localization (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A]
    (N : ℕ) (hN : 0 < N) (hA : (N : A) = 0)
    (t : OrdinaryFiniteTwistTransport A N hA) (S : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian S]
    (hS : IsUnit (N : Γ(S, ⊤))) (D : OrdinaryFiniteP1Datum A N hA t S hS)
    (K : DerivedCategoryModule A S) :
    let F := ordinaryFinitePushforward A (ProjectiveLine S ↘ S)
    let J := affineTraceOpenAdjunction A S
    let M := (ordinaryFiniteP1Right A N hA S).obj K
    ∃ (B : DerivedCategoryModule A S) (r : F.obj M ⟶ B)
      (w : B ⟶ ((affineTraceLineLeft A S).obj
        ((affineTraceLineRight A N hA S).obj K))⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧)
      (b : B ⊞ K ≅ F.obj M),
      Triangle.mk (F.map (J.counit.app M)) r w ∈ distTriang _ ∧
        biprod.inl ≫ b.hom ≫ r = 𝟙 B ∧ b.hom ≫ D.adjunction.counit.app K = biprod.snd
